key_assumptions.input: Starting free cash flow per share
key_assumptions.source: FY2025 free cash flow $884M ÷ ~334M shares (10-K FY2025)
AI workload growth; partial operating leverage
[Assumption] FCF scales with 30%+ product growth and margin expansion

open_questions: Confirm live price after post-earnings volatility (~$240 May 28, 2026).
Moat **unproven**: upgrade after two more quarters of retention and margin proof.
thesis: Snowflake runs a cloud data platform: customers store and analyze data on consumption-based contracts. **[Fact]** Product revenue (usage of the platform) drives economics; professional services are small. **[Fact]** FY2025 total revenue was **$3.63 billion** (+29% year-over-year); product revenue **$3.46 billion** (+30%). **[Fact]** FY2025 free cash flow was **$884 million** on **~334 million** shares (~**$2.65** per share). **[Fact]** Q1 fiscal 2027 (ended April 30, 2026) revenue was **$1.39 billion** (+33% year-over-year) per the earnings release. The company is positioning the platform as the **AI Data Cloud** (Cortex, Snowflake Intelligence).
why_market_wrong: **Predictive attribute:** none (no dated payoff). **[Inference]** After Q1 FY27 results (May 27, 2026), the stock re-rated sharply (~**$240** vs pre-earnings ~$175). The market may be extrapolating AI workload growth without modeling consumption volatility or stock-based compensation. Our base case uses **FY2025 free cash flow per share** as starting owner cash, not the post-rally multiple alone.
